title: First arrivals: Proof strip
summary: Set membership. Return the whole list.
descriptionMd:
Inputs
`readings` is a list of integers (numbers with no decimal part). It may be empty, and numbers may repeat unless task 1 says otherwise.

Your tasks
1. Create a list `firstCopies`. Keep the first copy of each number in `readings`. Skip any later copies of the same number. Keep the order in which the numbers first appear. For [4, 2, 4, 3, 2], `firstCopies` is [4, 2, 3].
2. Complete `firstArrivalsProofStrip` so it returns `firstCopies`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `readings` is [7, -3, 8, 9, 9], then `firstCopies` is [7, -3, 8, 9] and `firstArrivalsProofStrip` returns [7, -3, 8, 9].

Rules
- If `firstCopies` is empty, return [].

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `readings` is [0, 3, -10, 11, 3].
TEST DATA 2: `readings` is [7, 7, -6, 7].

constraints: Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
Input numbers have no decimal part. They range from -1,000,000 to 1,000,000. Follow any extra input rules in task 1.
Efficiency goal: time O(n); extra memory, including the helper list, O(n). n is the input length. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.
hints: Work through TEST DATA 1 by hand. Write down `firstCopies` before you look for the answer.

Return `firstCopies` once it is complete. If `firstCopies` is empty, return [].
